description: Formalize the explored term-2 to term-3 delayed-completion history for C_STALE_APPEND_COMPLETION. Compare node 3 unstable offset immediately before and after each actual held-response Step. Include current-term HardState-only and entry-bearing responses as permitted controls, and drain all work independently of property success.

harness.description: Three serialized RawNodes, ordered MemoryStorage worker model, actual elections/proposal/messages, finite delay of node 3 local entry-completion responses. Each response has produced/admitted/completed events with independent marker identity.
semantic_changes: No implementation edits. Same-package read-only access observes raft term, committed/applied indexes and unstable offset.
MemoryStorage substitutes for noncrashing stable storage; it is not an instrumented disk implementation.
Normal-entry application is modeled as immediate ordered no-op application before returning its attached completion; no state-machine payload effects are claimed.

legality.derivation: For unit-C_STALE_APPEND_COMPLETION, instantiate three RawNodes with AsyncStorageWrites and a consistent supplied restart prefix at index/term 1 and voters 1,2,3. S_API permits initialization from Storage; S_INIT consumes its saved state. MemoryStorage ApplySnapshot/SetHardState construct that explicit prefix; it is an assumed valid initial history, not a claim to have executed its consensus production. Campaign node 1 and pump actual Ready messages, then propose one normal entry, delay node 3 storage completion responses, campaign node 2, and pump all other work. Every held marker is the unmodified response attached by the implementation to actual MsgStorageAppend, saved only after processing its entries and HardState in per-node Ready order. S_CONFIG allows independently asynchronous completion; all held responses are finally delivered in original production order. Network append/vote replies are sent only after that modeled storage work completes. Step calls, Ready calls and campaigns are serialized on one test goroutine. No target state is assigned and no remote protocol response is synthesized. Entry payload application is a no-op model because the claim endpoint is unstable-prefix consumption, with only normal entries and no application-dependent decision. Tick omission is a finite event schedule; explicit campaigns perform actual elections and CheckQuorum is disabled. Persistence is MemoryStorage with no crash, not a physical disk assertion. Every admitted marker is stepped unconditionally and then observed, regardless of whether the forbidden truncation happens. The final pump is bounded separately from the property.
legality.applicability: Same RawNode objects survive the term transition. Snapshot-free responses only; no runtime snapshot or membership changes. Prior successful exploration supplies schedule feasibility, not correctness. RawNode is the selected entry, so Node goroutine channel semantics and synchronous Ready ordering disagreements are not permissions relied upon here.
alternatives: An overwrite/ABA history could test wider consequences, but is unnecessary for the documented stale-response no-truncation contract and remains excluded.

grounding.derivation: C_STALE_APPEND_COMPLETION is compared at synchronous RawNode.Step return. Each held response receives a unique marker_id at its actual production (after storage processing), independent of its term/index tuple or the compared offset. The produced prerequisite establishes actual origin and modeled storage completion. The admitted prerequisite records the receiving raft term and unstable offset immediately before Step, and references produced response_term to establish predecessor correlation; identity_fields associates node and marker_id exactly once. The completed result is emitted only after Step returns for that same saved response. The stale antecedent is calculated from the raw message Term and receiving raft Term before Step, not from the observed offset. A stale result must retain the admitted unstable_offset. This compares the documented no-truncation consequence directly: unstable.stableTo removes the prefix by increasing offset. No other event interleaves within Step and snapshot handling is excluded. Fresh responses remain observed as permitted controls without asserting all fresh markers must change offset; duplicate fresh completion is permitted. Final application progress is diagnostic only.
grounding.applicability: The comparison covers real returned markers in this bounded no-replacement, no-crash history. Output events include raw terms/indexes as audit context. Admission requires snapshot_free and the producer event storage_completed. All admitted operations owe completed observations; missing completion is not a holds result.
alternatives: Current-term responses whose entry term is old must remain permissible. Therefore only stale raft-term responses activate the safety assertion.

observable_properties.description: If the delivered marker was stale at admission, consuming it must not truncate the unstable entry prefix.

uncertainties: MemoryStorage and a consistent supplied snapshot prefix do not establish physical durability or a process-birth history.
No suffix replacement, runtime snapshot, crash or end-to-end client consistency consequence is checked.
Unstable offset is the selected prefix-truncation observable; payload preservation and arbitrary state mutation are outside this proposition.
